review.scope: Weekly review of Republican campaign preparation, congressional oversight, the air traffic shutdown and Venezuelan election negotiations. Full filings, court orders and election results remain incompletely checked.

administration.headline: Trump’s choice to lead the Republican Party faces a challenge after the midterms
administration.summary: Democrats are projected to control both chambers of Congress in January. After the defeats, Republican National Committee deputy KC Crosbie challenged party chair Joe Gruters and called for a review of what went wrong. Gruters defended his spending to committee members, and President Donald Trump backed him. The committee’s January vote will test whether Trump can keep his choice in charge of national party fundraising and campaign operations. In Congress, Democratic investigators face White House and Justice Department pressure as they prepare to lead committees. Axios reported that U.S. attorney Aaron Reitz asked Senator Elizabeth Warren to preserve records concerning her inquiries. The House sent Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s impeachment resolution to the Judiciary Committee. Pakistan says it is awaiting a U.S. reply to Iran’s proposals. Commerce released rules for licensing some remote uses of advanced U.S. chips. Senator Maria Cantwell asked Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to stop advanced chip diversion to China. House Democrats are weighing action on Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. as senators seek records on his testimony and gifts. After the Federal Aviation Administration halted departures nationwide, Representative Rick Larsen said he would revive committee investigators to scrutinize the agency’s modernization program. Further reporting is needed on Alaska’s final results, the immigration and tariff court cases, and Venezuela’s election timetable.

contests.title: Miller reportedly starts as White House chief of staff after Wiles’s departure
contests.assessment: Miller gains the staff-management role that Wiles held. Republican Representative Marlin Stutzman’s public criticism challenges the promotion after the election defeat, while Vance and Rubio have publicly welcomed it. Those contrasting reactions show disagreement among officials, not the balance of Republican voter opinion.
contests.authority: Trump chooses his chief of staff; Miller reportedly began November 9.
contests.leverage: The chief of staff manages access to Trump and senior White House work. Wiles may still advise Trump through his political team, but her new responsibilities remain unclear.
contests.change: The announced handover is now reported as completed. Its policy consequences and Wiles’s new responsibilities remain open.

basis.actions: The official appointment is followed by reporting that Miller began November 9.
basis.positions: Vance and Rubio welcomed Miller; Stutzman publicly opposed the promotion. The full CNN episode was not reviewed.
basis.money: No evidence establishes that a payment caused the appointment. Wiles’s possible influence over campaign funds must be checked separately from her White House job.

contests.watch: Check Miller’s written instructions and staffing choices, Wiles’s political responsibilities and further Republican defenses or criticism.
contests.summary: Stephen Miller reportedly began the chief-of-staff job on November 9. That gives him more ability to manage White House staff; Wiles’s political role remains unclear.

contests.title: Trump redirects Vance from Iran talks and says the United States does not need a deal
contests.assessment: Trump’s public instruction narrows Vance’s role in seeking an agreement. Rubio has defended the war on security grounds and has reportedly advocated sustained pressure.
contests.authority: Trump makes executive military decisions. Congress can authorize military action and decide funding; negotiations also require agreement from the other side.
contests.leverage: Officials negotiating with Iran can shape the terms presented to Trump. Advisers arguing for more military pressure can offer competing options. Public criticism can change who receives blame even before policy changes.
contests.change: Pakistan’s foreign minister Ishaq Dar said on November 16 that his government would continue mediating and was waiting for a U.S. response. His remarks show a route for exchanging proposals after Trump redirected Vance.

basis.actions: Trump redirected Vance publicly on November 12. Qatar had previously sought terms, and Axios reported Rubio’s account of sustained pressure to allies.
basis.positions: Vance criticized the war’s electoral cost. Rubio defended Trump’s initial decision and reportedly advocated continued pressure.
basis.money: Deal-Capital’s business exposure is relevant context, not proof of donor direction of negotiations.

contests.watch: Check who conducts the next contact with Qatar or Iran, whether Trump authorizes new operations, and what Vance is asked to do domestically.
contests.summary: Trump redirected Vice President JD Vance toward domestic issues. Pakistan’s foreign minister says he is awaiting a U.S. response to Iranian proposals, leaving open who will answer for Washington.

contests.title: Vance and his rivals compete for Trump’s voters, donors and campaign teams
contests.assessment: Vance’s Republican fundraising role and connections to donors and activist organizations could help him start a presidential campaign quickly. Rubio and other rivals have their own relationships and reasons to run. Public praise, donor interest and a formal endorsement are different levels of commitment.
contests.authority: Republican primary voters and convention delegates select the nominee. Trump can endorse a candidate and encourage his supporters to back that person, but he does not select the nominee on his own.
contests.leverage: Fundraisers can supply campaign money; activists can recruit volunteers; endorsements can help voters choose among candidates. A relationship helps only if the people involved actually commit support.
contests.change: KC Crosbie’s bid puts Trump’s choice of party chair to a committee vote in January. Axios reported that Vance might wait until spring to say whether he will run, on a timetable people familiar with his thinking said preceded the election. Gruters still chairs the committee, and Vance’s finance role continues to give him access to donors.

basis.actions: The RNC finance role, Malik fundraiser and Turning Point backing are concrete channels.
basis.positions: Public deferral, message support and a candidate endorsement mean different things.
basis.money: Thiel’s historical backing and Rockbridge access help explain Vance’s network; Griffin’s reported preference is not a Rubio contribution pledge.

contests.watch: Watch for announced campaigns, endorsements, committed funding, named organizers in early-primary states and voter surveys.
contests.summary: Vance has the strongest documented fundraising and activist connections among the tracked candidates. Rubio and other rivals could recruit some of the same supporters; Trump has not settled the race.

contests.title: Trump’s attempt to remove Lisa Cook faces legal challenges
contests.assessment: Trump’s effort to remove Cook could affect who serves on the Federal Reserve’s governing board. Courts and the required hearing process limit how that effort proceeds. Interest-rate decisions still belong to the Federal Open Market Committee, which includes Federal Reserve governors and regional bank presidents.
contests.authority: The Federal Open Market Committee votes on interest rates. The dispute over Cook’s removal involves the president, the courts and the procedures required by law.
contests.leverage: White House officials can press for a change in Fed leadership or lower rates. Treasury officials can advise on the market consequences, but neither group can simply order the committee to change its rate vote.
contests.change: The Supreme Court refused in June to lift the order that kept Cook in office while the case proceeds. A later White House hearing was delayed. A new ruling or completed hearing remains unverified.

basis.actions: The hearing was delayed; the later filing addressed scheduling and participation.
basis.positions: Calls for lower rates do not establish a changed vote or removal.
basis.money: Market exposure can explain interests; no payment causing a rate decision is established.

contests.watch: Check the hearing date, court orders, any final removal decision and the committee’s actual rate votes.
contests.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook remained in office under a court order while Trump pursued a separate White House inquiry. The hearing date and any decision to remove her remain open.

contests.title: Congress presses for Epstein records as the White House challenges planned investigations
contests.summary: Massie’s petition gives House members a way to seek a vote on access to Epstein records. White House counsel warned Representative Robert Garcia over planned investigations. Garcia pledged to proceed.
contests.assessment: Attorney General Todd Blanche controls how the Justice Department responds to demands for records, subject to law and court orders. Representative Thomas Massie’s bill would give survivors, state prosecutors and lawmakers a way to sue for records they believe the department unlawfully withheld. The White House warning gives Republicans a public argument against the inquiries. Garcia’s public reply shows he intends to proceed. Incoming committee chairs will decide which requests to pursue first.
contests.authority: The attorney general directs the Justice Department. Different jobs may require presidential appointment, Senate confirmation or a temporary acting appointment.
contests.leverage: The Justice Department manages its records and can contest demands in court. House members can seek floor time through the petition. Incoming committee chairs can schedule hearings and pursue records through their committees.
contests.change: U.S. attorney Aaron Reitz extended his requests to Senator Elizabeth Warren after asking Senator Richard Blumenthal to preserve records. Warren’s inquiries include how tech companies benefit from tax breaks for AI investments. Blumenthal had asked Reitz for his own records. A reply to Blumenthal or a decision to pursue charges remains unverified.

basis.actions: The House clerk recorded 218 signatures. The Associated Press reported the White House warning and Garcia’s public reply.
basis.positions: The White House defended its prior release of records. Garcia says Congress will exercise its oversight authority.
basis.money: The White House warning and the petition do not establish that a financial relationship drove a particular records decision.

contests.watch: Check for a floor motion, the actual roll call and how Blanche responds to a specific request from a committee or court.

contests.title: House sends the bid to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to committee
contests.summary: The House voted 211–204 to send Representative Thomas Massie’s resolution to the Judiciary Committee. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth remains in office.
contests.assessment: The vote showed that nearly all Republicans who voted favored keeping the articles off the floor at this stage. Democrats are projected to control the House in January and could revisit the allegations.
contests.authority: The Judiciary Committee controls what happens next to this resolution. The House can adopt articles of impeachment. The Senate would decide conviction in a separate proceeding.
contests.leverage: Trump publicly backs Hegseth. Massie can point voters who want Congress to check the president’s war powers to a recorded vote.
contests.change: Axios reported that Representative Delia Ramirez and Representative-elect Melat Kiros publicly questioned Democratic leadership’s performance after floor setbacks that included the Hegseth referral. Axios also attributed criticism to unnamed Democrats. Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries pointed to a veterans bill his party brought to a successful vote through a discharge petition.

basis.actions: The House voted 211–204 to send the resolution to committee.
basis.positions: The White House opposed impeachment. Massie was the only Republican to vote against sending the resolution to committee.
basis.money: The available evidence establishes how members voted.

contests.watch: Watch for Judiciary Committee action and whether incoming House leaders schedule another vote. Check whether senators publicly commit to a position on specific articles.

nomination.headline: Vance leads, but rivals could win Republicans unhappy with Trump’s record.
nomination.summary: Vice President JD Vance leads the Republican nomination forecast. Reuters reported that Texas Senator Ted Cruz has started preparing for a 2028 run, giving him time to recruit while Vance and Florida Governor Ron DeSantis weigh when to decide. Their prospects depend in part on whether Republican voters want a change in the approach to the Iran war and rising household costs.

candidates.path: Axios reports that Vance may wait until spring to declare. His advisers can still recruit quietly, but Cruz can offer early-state activists work sooner.
candidates.coalition: Vance could retain Trump-aligned voters who want tighter immigration rules and relief from war and household costs. Existing Republican fundraising and activist relationships could help recruit staff and volunteers, but an introduction or endorsement does not guarantee votes.
candidates.advantage: Vance can use a domestic assignment to speak to Republican voters about crime and government conduct if he is given a role with visible results.
candidates.vulnerability: Waiting gives Cruz time to recruit. Vance can limit that cost if his advisers keep donors and organizers on board while he weighs how to handle his relationship with Trump.
candidates.positions: Vance favors tighter immigration rules and economic policies presented as helping American workers and families. He has also argued for negotiations over Iran; that does not erase his earlier public support for administration decisions.
candidates.money: Peter Thiel previously financed Vance’s political rise. Rockbridge and other Republican fundraising relationships could help a campaign, but past support does not establish a new 2028 commitment.

candidates.path: Reuters found several donors who want Rubio in the race. He would need to enter, recruit a team and explain the decisions he made as secretary of state.
candidates.coalition: Some Republican donors want Rubio to run. Robert Bigelow also likes Vance, and Cruz can ask overlapping donors to back a campaign that starts sooner.
candidates.advantage: Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended the original decision to fight Iran and reportedly argued for continued pressure. Trump’s move away from Vance’s talks gives Rubio more room to make that case, with the next negotiating or military decisions still open.
candidates.vulnerability: Donor interest overlaps with Vance and Cruz, and it could stay a preference without money or staff.
candidates.positions: Rubio has defended Trump’s decision to use force against Iran. He could argue that pressure on U.S. adversaries is necessary, but voters may judge him by the war’s costs and results.
candidates.money: Some donors have expressed interest in Rubio. A reported preference is not the same as a pledge to finance his presidential campaign.

candidates.path: Reuters reported that DeSantis is exploring a campaign but could wait until 2032. Florida organizers offer a starting point if he enters.
candidates.coalition: DeSantis could recruit social conservatives and Republicans seeking an experienced governor. Former campaign staff and donors offer a starting point for rebuilding, but they can choose Kemp or another rival instead.
candidates.advantage: He can present a record of carrying out conservative policies as evidence that he would act decisively. Axios reported that Florida Governor Ron DeSantis has pointed to his party’s victories in Florida as a model for recovering after the midterms.
candidates.vulnerability: Early conversations could reflect genuine preparation. A named presidential team would distinguish it from keeping his options open.
candidates.positions: His record includes conservative policies enacted in Florida. His support for limited military strikes means that distance from the White House does not necessarily mean opposition to intervention abroad.
candidates.money: DeSantis has raised substantial money for past campaigns. That shows fundraising experience, but does not establish which donors would back another presidential bid.

candidates.path: Conservative economist Stephen Moore told Reuters that Senator Ted Cruz said he intended to run for president. Cruz could use the time before other candidates decide to contact Iowa activists who know him.
candidates.coalition: Cruz could recruit social conservatives and Republicans who want limits on the Iran war. He competes with Vance for activists and with Rubio for donors who value national experience.
candidates.advantage: Cruz won Iowa’s Republican caucuses in 2016. An early decision to run could give him a chance to call activists who worked with him before other campaigns hire them.
candidates.vulnerability: Cruz’s Iowa contacts give him a place to start. He would still have to win voters outside that group, especially if Trump backs Vance.
candidates.positions: Cruz generally favors a forceful foreign policy but has criticized tariffs. These positions may attract different groups of Republican voters rather than one united base.
candidates.money: Donors supported Cruz in earlier presidential contests. We have not established that those relationships will become financial commitments for 2028.

candidates.path: John McEntee could ask people he worked with in Trump’s first-term personnel office and in Project 2025 to help build a campaign. He can already reach viewers through his conservative media business.
candidates.coalition: McEntee could seek culturally conservative Trump supporters who want first-term policies with a different leader. His media audience could introduce him to potential supporters, while former personnel contacts might help recruit campaign specialists. Neither shows that people will donate, volunteer or vote for him.
candidates.advantage: Informal political communication could make an unfamiliar candidate approachable to some conservative viewers.
candidates.vulnerability: People McEntee helped recruit for government posts would have to choose to join a presidential campaign. His online audience gives him a way to reach potential supporters. Its willingness to vote or volunteer remains unknown.
candidates.positions: His first-term record includes support for restrictive immigration staffing and troop withdrawals. That record does not establish every position he would take in a presidential campaign today.
candidates.money: Technology investor Peter Thiel invested in McEntee’s dating business. That was a business investment, not a confirmed presidential-campaign contribution or endorsement.

candidates.path: Paul has said he is considering a run. He can ask old campaign contacts and antiwar activists to organize around Congress’s authority over military action.
candidates.coalition: Paul could recruit Republicans who want limits on spending and presidential war powers. His support for Massie shows cooperation despite Trump’s opposition, but a presidential contest could divide their overlapping activists and donors. A third-party effort could compete for some antiwar organizers; Paul would still have to persuade them to join his Republican campaign.
candidates.advantage: Paul can criticize the administration’s use of military power and still work with Senate Republicans. He publicly rejected blaming John Thune for state-level election results after Republicans lost the Senate majority.
candidates.vulnerability: Republicans who want the war ended could credit an official who delivers a deal or stay with Trump while urging a policy change.
candidates.positions: Paul advocates limits on executive power, lower federal spending and freer trade. The review has not established all the immigration policies he would propose in a new presidential campaign.
candidates.money: Paul has historical links to the Protect Freedom political group and donor Jeff Yass. Those connections do not establish a confirmed financial commitment to a 2028 presidential bid.

candidates.path: Kemp has reportedly weighed a campaign. He could ask Georgia donors and organizers to help him build a team outside the state.
candidates.coalition: Kemp’s Georgia supporters and state political relationships offer a base from which to recruit outside the state. Republicans looking for a governor could also choose DeSantis; Georgia approval does not establish national presidential preference.
candidates.advantage: He can use concrete governing examples and personal experience to make a restrained executive pitch.
candidates.vulnerability: A choice to wait or local loyalties that stop at the state line would limit the value of his Georgia network.
candidates.positions: His Georgia record includes tax cuts and conservative immigration, policing and social policies. A state record does not establish a complete presidential platform.
candidates.money: This review has not verified commitments from donors to finance a Kemp presidential campaign.

candidates.path: Massie can point to forcing a vote on the Hegseth resolution. Libertarian recruiters offer a separate party route, and he has not committed to it.
candidates.coalition: Massie could recruit Republicans who value his challenges to presidential war-making and his oversight efforts. Past House-race fundraising shows some willingness to act, but Paul competes for overlapping supporters and Massie has not settled on a Republican presidential campaign. An external recruiting effort may draw organizers away from a Republican bid, but his choice and his supporters’ choices remain open.
candidates.advantage: Massie secured enough signatures to seek a House vote on a second Epstein records bill. The petition gives him a concrete example of working with Democrats on disclosure while opposing the Trump administration on other issues.
candidates.vulnerability: Coverage of a congressional vote or outside draft can raise his visibility without yielding Republican delegates.
candidates.positions: Massie has pushed for congressional approval of military action and disclosure of government records. The review has not established a complete current presidential platform.
candidates.money: Groups spent money supporting Massie in his House primary. That does not establish that he controls those funds or that the same groups would finance a presidential campaign.

recovery.title: Peace and lower household costs restore Republican confidence in Trump’s allies
recovery.summary: War conditions and household costs improve enough that Republican voters regain confidence in Trump’s allies. Later disclosures do not undo that recovery.

managed_costs.title: Republican voters stay with Trump’s allies despite anger over costs
managed_costs.summary: Republican voters remain unhappy with costs and policy results, but neither investigations nor a rival campaign persuades enough of them to abandon Trump’s allies. Existing campaign relationships help those allies remain competitive.

systemic.title: Republican voters blame senior Trump officials and look for a new leader
systemic.summary: Continuing policy failures or credible disclosures persuade a consequential group of Republican voters to blame senior Trump officials. Those voters reject an explanation that blames only subordinates and look for different leadership.

selective.title: Republican voters keep backing Trump while demanding changes from his successor
selective.summary: Republican voters continue to support Trump while asking his successor to replace particular officials or change policies like the approach to Iran. Candidates gain support if voters trust them to make those changes.

backlash.title: Republican voters rally behind Trump’s allies against Democratic investigations
backlash.summary: Democratic investigations fail to persuade enough Republican voters. Conflict with Democrats becomes a stronger reason to support Trump’s allies, even though policy results have not substantially improved.

cross_implications.title: Vance’s war criticism could help him compete with Rubio.
cross_implications.assessment: Vance can argue that he wants to end a war Rubio has defended. Rivals can also point to Vance’s earlier public defenses of the administration and question when he changed his position. The statement alone does not show which candidate voters now prefer.

cross_implications.title: Miller could shape which advisers and proposals reach Trump.
cross_implications.assessment: Miller reportedly began as chief of staff November 9. Candidates seeking Trump’s help may have to work with his staff, but no 2028 endorsement follows from the appointment.

cross_implications.title: Justice Department departures could strengthen Blanche while Miller gains a White House role.
cross_implications.assessment: Blanche may be able to choose replacements and direct managers after the reported departures. Miller’s prospective White House role gives him a different way to influence decisions. Neither change alone proves that investigations will stop or policy will change.

cross_implications.title: Trump redirects Vance after his criticism of the Iran war
cross_implications.assessment: Vance can still argue that the Iran war hurt Republicans. Trump’s November 12 instruction makes a diplomatic result harder for Vance to deliver. Actual domestic responsibilities and voter reaction remain open.

cross_implications.title: Massie’s Epstein petition shows how Republicans can work with Democrats on disclosure
cross_implications.assessment: Four Republicans joined 214 Democrats on the petition. That gives Massie and other Republicans who challenge Trump a concrete example to show disclosure advocates. Support for the proposal and willingness to recruit for a Republican presidential campaign remain separate questions.

relationships.kind: Different positions on the Iran war
relationships.assessment: Vance’s argument for ending the war competes with the position of advisers who defend military pressure. That gives voters a difference to judge; it does not establish that support has already moved from one candidate to another.

relationships.kind: Miller replaces Wiles as White House chief of staff
relationships.assessment: Miller reportedly began November 9, taking the White House staff-management role from Wiles. Her continuing influence depends on political responsibilities that remain unclear.

relationships.kind: Investors and fundraisers with past links to Vance
relationships.assessment: Past financial backing and fundraising relationships could help Vance recruit money and staff. They do not establish agreement with him on every policy or a new commitment to a presidential campaign.

power_shifts.role_change: Miller has reportedly replaced Wiles as chief of staff; her political responsibilities remain unclear.
power_shifts.implication: Wiles no longer holds the reported White House staff-management role. A continued political relationship may preserve influence, but her responsibilities and authority over campaign money remain unverified.

power_shifts.role_change: Miller reportedly began as White House chief of staff on November 9.
power_shifts.implication: Miller now has the reported staff-management role, which can help him decide which officials and proposals reach Trump. Specific new policy instructions and results remain unverified.

power_method.title: How the access ratings work
power_method.scale: The scale compares jobs, not measured shares of political power: 0 means no identified way to influence the decision; 1 means an outside adviser; 2 means a role in Trump’s political team; 3 means a deputy White House role; 4 means the chief of staff; 5 means the president, who makes the final executive decision.
power_method.status: The 0–5 ratings compare the access associated with the jobs. Miller’s start is reported; the ratings are analytical judgments, not measured shares or probabilities.
power_method.condition: Reporting supports Miller’s November 9 start. The 0–5 ratings compare access associated with the jobs, not measured overall power. Wiles’s political responsibilities and the policy effects remain unresolved.
power_method.policy_projection: Miller could use the chief-of-staff job to prioritize immigration enforcement and staff who favor it. That does not establish that the Iran war will escalate: the record also includes reporting that Miller argued for an exit. Incoming Democratic majorities could demand records and challenge funding once the new Congress begins.
